comments.author: @PixelTomorrow
comments.text:
Corruption, laws and regulations, education, and other issues in Indonesia are only temporary. Many countries used to face these exact same problems and managed to overcome them. Indonesia can do it too.

Technology and progress also shift from one country to another. We all know of nations that used to be superpowers, yet are no longer so today.

True wealth lies in big land mass, fertile land, rich natural and cultural resources, big population, patriotic citizens, and national unity. GDP, GDP per capita, or other metrics that define a "rich" country can always change. Indonesia can achieve that too.

Other countries of a similar scale and population—such as the USA, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria, or Brazil—also experienced ups and downs during their first 81 years of independence. Moreover, developing Indonesia is the most challenging among all these nations due to its geography of thousands of islands, unlike countries such as the USA or Brazil, which sit on a single massive landmass.

As an Indonesian citizen nearing 50 years of age, I have personally experienced just how much progress Indonesia has made in politics, the economy, socio-cultural aspects, and beyond. I believe Indonesia is in the right track to be a great nation, just need to eradicate those temporary problems.

The Indonesian rupiah has fallen from around 8,469 per USD in 2003 to 18,073 in 2026. That's a 53.14% loss in its value against the dollar over 23 years. In other words, the USD now buys about 113.40% more rupiah than it did back then. It's sad to see the rupiah keep melting away. 😅 
     Looking at the bigger picture, Indonesia still managed to maintain a cumulative account surplus of US$2.05 billion between 2022 and Q3 2026. That's actually quite encouraging!
     The massive commodity boom in 2022, which generated a surplus of US$13.2 billion, helped offset the combined deficits from 2023 to 2025. Even after a historic US$12.49 billion drop in Q2 2026, largely due to volatile energy import costs, Indonesia managed to bounce back into a small surplus in Q3.
